newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ASTROS REPLACE MANAGER COLLINS WITH BROADCASTER.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ASTROS REPLACE MANAGER COLLINS WITH BROADCASTER.

text.p: The Houston Astros on Friday fired manager Terry Collins and replaced him with veteran broadcaster Larry Dierker.
Dierker, 50, a former pitcher with no previous coaching experience, had been a radio and television colour analyst for Astros' games since 1979.

General Manager Gerry Hunsicker acknowledged at a news conference to announce the change that the choice of Dierker was "somewhat unconventional," but said his "insight and knowledge of the game is second to none."
"We believe Larry is a special individual who is uniquely qualified for the position," Hunsicker said.
"His familiarity with our organisation and ballclub gives him a big advantage in assuming this position."

Dierker began his big-league career with the Astros, then known as the Colt .45s, in 1964 and was twice an All-Star before finishing with the St Louis Cardinals in 1977. He moved into the broadcast booth in 1979.
"I know the players and what they can and perhaps can't do...if you brought somebody in from another team they would have to go into spring training and learn the players," Dierker said.
Collins led the Astros to second-place finishes all three years that he managed in Houston.
His fate was likely sealed when he presided over a September swoon that saw the Astros lose nine consecutive games to fall out of playoff contention.
The Astros finished the season 82-80, six games behind the Central Division-winning St Louis Cardinals and eight games behind the wild card Los Angeles Dodgers.
"We just felt that a change was necessary for this organisation to move forward," Hunsicker said.
